title: Burst-aware continuous batching conductor: workload profiling, heuristics, and safe apply/rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a production-ready recommendation engine (the 'Conductor') that suggests and safely applies continuous batching parameters and KV/prefix caching policies for workloads that exhibit bursty traffic and mixed sequence-length distributions. Scope: workload profiling collection, heuristic model design, simulation sandbox, canary apply path, automated rollback triggers, and observability surfaces for cost/latency/regressions.

Background: Current autotune works well for steady-state traffic but tends to either over-batch during sudden bursts (increasing latency) or under-batch during microbursts (increasing cost). This ticket focuses on a burst-aware approach that balances latency SLOs and token-unit cost while enabling safe automated config changes.

Success metrics:
- 12%-20% token cost reduction for targeted workloads without increasing 95th pct latency beyond SLO (default SLO = 250ms).
- Rollback rate < 2% for automated applies during first 4 weeks of rollout.
- Clear per-workload and cluster-level dashboard showing before/after cost and latency.

Design decisions and heuristics (summary):
- Profile inputs: sequence length histograms (p50/p90/p99), inter-arrival time distributions, request size, model variant, prefix reuse rate, peak-to-base ratio.
- Heuristic scoring: combine 'cost-sensitivity' (expected token savings from batch increase) and 'latency-risk' (probability of breaching latency SLO given current queueing headroom). Use conservative weightings during initial rollout (alpha=0.6 latency-risk, beta=0.4 cost).
- Continuous parameter annealing: propose discrete steps for max_batch_size and batch_timeout_ms with cooldown windows (default cooldown = 15m) to avoid oscillation.
- KV/prefix caching recommendation: if prefix reuse > 15% and cache hit latency < 1ms, suggest enabling KV warmup + pinned cache entries for top-N prefixes.
- Burst handling: maintain a burst-protection cap that limits batch growth when recent arrival-rate variance > threshold.

Safety and rollout plan:
- Offline simulation harness (runtime-sim) using collected traces to estimate cost/latency impact for each candidate config.
- Staging canary with traffic shadowing for 24h, verifying metrics and custom eval prompts for quality regressions.
- Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with health gates at each step. Health gates: 95th latency, p99 memory, model output regression rate (from eval prompts).
- Automated rollback triggers: latency SLO breach > 10% relative increase, model quality regression > threshold, or error-rate spike (>2x baseline).

Observability:
- New dashboards: per-workload recommended vs active batch config, projected token savings, applied time-series, rollback events.
- Tracing hooks for sampled requests to correlate batch size -> per-token latency.
- Audit log entry for every automated apply/rollback with reason and metrics snapshot.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-62830 (draft)
- Runtime simulation repo: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-sim (PR #112)
